summary: The Round 1 reconstruction misplaces Witness B in the westbound lanes north of the intersection ([-4, 0, -29.3]), whereas the deposition video at 27:05–27:13 shows her marking Exhibit 4 with a red X on the southeast corner in front of the retail store near the bench shelter ([5.5, 0, 4.0]). When Witness B is placed at her actual marked position on the southeast corner and Vehicle T's left-turn position across the eastbound lanes is aligned with the physical evidence, the turning semitrailer blocks her line of sight to Vehicle A in the final second before impact, contradicting her testimony that nothing was in her way. The world module has been patched to place Witness B at her Exhibit 4 marked position, refine Vehicle T's turn keyframes, and prevent witness vehicles from self-occluding.

findings.summary: Witness B marked her position on Exhibit 4 on the southeast corner near the bench shelter ([5.5, 0, 4.0]), not in the westbound lanes ([-4, 0, -29.3]), and from her true position the turning semitrailer blocks her view of Vehicle A before impact.
findings.detail: In Round 1, the world module placed Witness B at [-4, 0, -29.3] in the westbound lanes on the north side of the highway, which artificially gave her an unobstructed sightline (Independent check: wit_B -> veh_A pass=true, distance 33.8 m). However, in evidence/deposition.mp4 at 27:05–27:13, Witness B places a red X on Exhibit 4 on the southeast corner of the intersection—on the eastbound shoulder/corner east of NE 140th Court and just northwest of the open-sided bench shelter in front of the retail store (approximately [5.5, 0, 4.0] per the Exhibit 4 scale bar), matching her testimony at Depo 09:05–09:20 and 27:04–27:36. From that southeast corner position, as Vehicle T's semitrailer crosses both eastbound lanes and enters NE 140th Court along x ≈ 0, the solid van body of the trailer (1.2–4.11 m high) stands directly between Witness B (x = 5.5 m, eyeHeight = 1.6 m) and oncoming eastbound Vehicle A (x < 0, z = 0) at t = 9.8 s, contradicting her claim at Depo 27:47–28:27 that she saw the front of the car clearly right up until impact with nothing in the way.

evidence.citation: SE corner bench shelter and scale bar (0-40 m)
sightline wit_B→veh_A: pass=true at erroneous position [-4, 1.6, -29.3]

findings.summary: Vehicle T's turn keyframes are refined so the tractor-semitrailer position at impact matches the 13.84 m tractor-front-to-impact offset and eliminates spline acceleration spikes.
findings.detail: Facts F15 and F16 state that the 21.82 m (71 ft 7 in) tractor-semitrailer combination was struck on the right side of the semitrailer about 13.84 m (45 ft 5 in) behind the front of the tractor in the outside eastbound lane (origin [0, 0, 0]). In Round 1, Vehicle T's tractor center at t = 10.43 s was placed at z = 5.2 m and the trailer center at z = -1.2 m, placing the tractor front ~5.3 m short of the documented 13.84 m offset and causing a 0.79 g Hermite spline acceleration peak between t = 8.0 s and t = 10.43 s. The Round 2 patch adjusts the tractor and trailer keyframes so the trailer spans across the eastbound lanes and NE 140th Court throat at t = 9.8–10.43 s and comes to rest south of the retail store on NE 140th Court as marked by Witness B at Depo 26:38–26:47.

findings.summary: Witness A's and Witness C's vehicles are set to non-occluding so they do not self-occlude their own driver sightlines during robustness sampling.
findings.detail: The Round 1 independent sightline checks for wit_A and wit_C passed from their nominal positions but reported partial robustness (1/25 blocked by veh_witA for Witness A; 2/25 blocked by veh_witC for Witness C) because their own vehicle meshes had occludes=true. Setting occludes=false on veh_witA and veh_witC prevents self-occlusion while preserving the scene geometry described in witness_A.txt and witness_C.txt.

evidence.citation: sightline wit_A→veh_A blocked 1/25 by veh_witA; sightline wit_C→veh_T_trailer blocked 2/25 by veh_witC

findings.summary: Vehicle A's pre-impact speed (74 mph), 10.43 s sight time from the vertical crest, absence of pre-impact braking or skid marks, and post-impact trajectory to the utility pole and final rest at 277 m match the record.
findings.detail: Vehicle A approaches eastbound from the vertical crest at x = -345 m (1,132 ft) at a constant 74 mph (33.08 m/s) with no braking or pre-impact skid marks, reaching the point of impact at t = 10.43 s, striking the utility pole 8.4 s later (t = 18.83 s), and coming to rest 277 m (910 ft) east of the POI. Both the timing check (10.43 s continuous line of sight for both drivers) and plausibility check confirm consistency with NTSB findings.

findings.summary: Daylight, clear sky, dry road surface, sun position (azimuth 265°, elevation 45.1° in the west), headlights-off state, and absence of sun glare are consistent with the documentary record; no real scene footage exists.
findings.detail: The collision occurred on May 7, 2016 at 16:36 EDT near Williston, Florida (approx. 29.39°N, 82.53°W) in clear daylight on a dry road with Vehicle A's headlights off (facts.txt F1–F4; police_report.txt p.1, p.3; Depo 09:25–10:18, 16:02). The world's environment sun is positioned in the west at azimuth 265.0° and elevation 45.1° (shadow bearing 85° east). Because the sun elevation (45.1°) exceeds the 30° glare threshold and is behind eastbound traffic, sun glare is not a factor for any witness or driver. No real scene photos or footage exist in the case file (only the simulated deposition video and schematic Exhibit 4 map), so lighting is compared against the documentary record and computed solar position only. Explicit date, coordinates, and UTC offset metadata have been added to world.meta.
